## Research approach

My work is grounded in the belief that better data leads to better health outcomes. By combining GIS and public health methods, I examine where and why inequalities in healthcare access exist, particularly for women and children. My research supports data-driven planning, helping decision-makers allocate resources more equitably and improve health service delivery.

My research sits at the crossroads of geographic data science and public health, with a particular interest in how location and distribution of quality health services influence health outcomes. I focus on:

```{=html}
<div class="topic-grid">
  <div class="topic"><p class="topic-h" role="heading" aria-level="3">Healthcare accessibility and utilisation<span class="tag-o">travel time</span></p><p>How far people live from care, and how distance and quality shape whether they use it.</p></div>
  <div class="topic"><p class="topic-h" role="heading" aria-level="3">Maternal, newborn and child health<span class="tag-o">EmONC</span></p><p>Where women give birth, who misses care, and how to bring quality services closer.</p></div>
  <div class="topic"><p class="topic-h" role="heading" aria-level="3">Spatial health inequalities<span class="tag-o">equity</span></p><p>Where health and health services differ across places, and who gets left behind.</p></div>
  <div class="topic"><p class="topic-h" role="heading" aria-level="3">Routine health data systems<span class="tag-o">DHIMS</span></p><p>Turning data health systems already collect into evidence for planning.</p></div>
  <div class="topic"><p class="topic-h" role="heading" aria-level="3">Spatial epidemiology and disease mapping<span class="tag-o">mapping</span></p><p>Mapping where disease occurs to show where risk is highest and where to act.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Collaborations and impact

I regularly collaborate with government health agencies, NGOs, and international partners to turn research into real-world solutions. My work has informed health strategies across low- and middle-income countries, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. My PhD, funded by the ESRC, was [recognised nationally](https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ukgwa/20260702125540/https://www.ukri.org/who-we-are/how-we-are-doing/research-outcomes-and-impact/esrc/improving-access-to-pregnancy-and-birth-services-in-ghana/) and [locally](https://southcoastdtp.ac.uk/news-post/the-scdtp-is-delighted-to-announce-the-winners-of-the-2020-21-and-2021-22-scdtp-impact-prizes-congratulations-to-all-winners/) for its impact on evidence-based policymaking and capacity development in Ghana.

```{=html}
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const buttons = document.querySelectorAll(".filters button");
  const pubs = document.querySelectorAll(".pub");
  buttons.forEach((b) => {
    const f = b.dataset.f;
    const n = f === "all" ? pubs.length : [...pubs].filter((p) => p.dataset.themes.split(" ").includes(f)).length;
    b.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", ` <span class="n">${n}</span>`);
    b.addEventListener("click", () => {
      buttons.forEach((x) => x.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(x === b)));
      pubs.forEach((p) => { p.hidden = f !== "all" && !p.dataset.themes.split(" ").includes(f); });
      document.querySelectorAll(".pub-group").forEach((g) => { g.hidden = !g.querySelector(".pub:not([hidden])"); });
    });
  });
});
</script>
```
